notes: TODAY'S VALUE FOR ai_horizon IS OUT OF DATE. 17.4 h (95% CI 8.48-55.07 h, Claude Mythos Preview early, released 2026-04-07, added to METR's page 8 May 2026; 80% horizon 3.10 h) is the last point on METR's Time Horizon 1.1 page, which says it is 'no longer actively updated' (last update 8 Sep 2026). METR's 20 Nov 2026 report, on a harder combined TH1.1+TH2 suite, gives GPT-6 Astra 40 h (95% CI 13-2,645) and Opus 5.5 39 h (12-1,253), and cites Fable 5.1 at about 30 h. The two suites are not directly comparable (TH2 is harder, so the same model scores lower on the combined suite). Recommend showing 40 h (Nov 2026, combined suite) with a caveat, or keeping 17.4 h labelled 'Apr 2026, TH1.1'.

Doubling times differ by source and period: METR TH1.1 data file, from 2023 on: 128.7 days (95% CI 104.4-158.0) = 4.2 months, excluding points above 16 h; all-time stitched: 187.8 days (6.2 months). Kwa et al. 2025 (2019-2025): 207 days (CI 166-240), about 7 months. METR Nov 2026 combined suite: 3.61 months (95% CI 2.08-4.94); it cites the previous TH1.1 trend as 105 days. TH2 verifiable subset alone: 1.65 months (CI 0.79-3.99), which METR says could indicate a 2026 acceleration but has other explanations.

CORRECTION to the brief: the 'about twice as fast as March 2024-October 2025' finding is from METR's 5 Nov 2026 Independent Assessment of AI R&D Acceleration at Anthropic. It concerns Anthropic's models on AECI (Anthropic's version of the Epoch Capabilities Index, a benchmark index), not time horizons: 1.9x (95% CI 1.5-2.8), with METR saying 1.3x-3x would not surprise it; across all frontier developers the acceleration was about 1.4x. METR's 20 Nov report found no strong acceleration on its own capability index across public frontier models.

METR measurement ceilings: TH1.1 values above 16 h are flagged unreliable; the combined suite's longest score threshold is 200 h; no human-timed tasks of 2,000 h exist. The 2,000 h exceedance therefore refers to the capability, not to a METR measurement. METR also says human baselines are getting hard to obtain and containerized tests may overstate real-world ability.

All ai_horizon exceedance values are judged. The only published-distribution input is Kwa et al. 2025 (one work-month mid-2029, 80% CI mid-2028 to mid-2030 on the 2019-2025 trend), which implies roughly 0.74 for 167 h by 2030 if treated as a normal distribution; measured progress since then has outpaced that trend, so the judged 0.88 is higher.

The 80% horizon is much shorter than the 50% horizon (Mythos Preview: 3.1 h vs 17.4 h). LEAP Wave 8 (Apr-May 2026): median expert gives 50% that a model reaches 80% success on 8-hour-plus software tasks by 2030; superforecasters' median year 2028. FRI's own accuracy review found LEAP experts underestimated recent AI progress.

Metaculus API requires authentication and the site blocks plain fetches, so Metaculus values were read on 24 Nov 2026 from the question pages (displayed estimate plus the embedded community CDF) in a browser. Q5121 median 30 Jan 2030 (IQR 28 Dec 2027 to 2 Apr 2035, 1,857 forecasters); Q3479 weak AGI median 17 Aug 2027 (1,735 forecasters); Q9062 weak-AGI-to-SI gap median 23.4 months (IQR 7.5-94.9 months, 352 forecasters), with 1.6% below one day (includes SI before weak AGI) and 8.9% beyond 50 years.

Metaculus-derived SI distribution (superintelligence exceedance, basis 'derived'): weak-AGI date CDF (Q3479) convolved with the gap CDF (Q9062), assuming independence. 30.5% of Q3479's CDF mass lies before today (stale or 'imminent' forecasts on a still-open question); it was treated as arriving now. Result: 2028 0.18, 2030 0.405, 2035 0.63, 2040 0.72, 2050 0.80, 2075 0.87, 2100 0.88; median mid-2031, IQR mid-2028 to early 2043. Scripts: scratchpad/scripts/si_convolve2.py with data in scratchpad/raw/dl_metaculus/.

Year convention for superintelligence thresholds: Metaculus and Manifold values are 'before 1 January of that year'; XPT, Epoch and ESPAI values are 'by that year' as the source states; AI Futures 'before 2028' = by end of 2027.

Definitions behind each SI number, weakest to strongest: Metaculus Q3479 weak AGI (lowest bar); XPT 'Nick Bostrom affirms AGI exists'; Metaculus Q5121 general AI (Turing test, robotics, expert benchmark, coding); LEAP AGI (beats 90th-percentile professionals in every non-physical job at 90% of tasks, under 5x human cost); ESPAI high-level machine intelligence (every task better and cheaper than human workers, feasibility not adoption); Epoch 'transformative AI'; AI Futures TED-AI (better than top experts at virtually all tasks); Metaculus Q9062 superintelligence (any task humans could do in 2021, as well as the best humans) and Manifold 'superintelligence' (undefined). Only the last group matches the site's SI definition; none requires wide deployment.

ESPAI 2024 also asked how likely 'vastly better than humans at all professions' AI is after HLMI: median 10% within 2 years, 60% within 30 years (means 20.9% and 59.6%). Full automation of labor: 10% by 2035, 50% by 2098. The 2023 survey text gives only 10% and 50% HLMI years (2027, 2047); other percentiles appear only in charts and were not used.

Epoch AI: the only Epoch aggregate found is the Jan 2023 literature review. Epoch researcher Ege Erdil (Apr 2025, personal view, not Epoch's) gives a ~20-year median for full automation of remote work and about 30% within 10 years.

ai_loss_of_control projections use 'value' = probability (0-1), not a factor level; superintelligence projections use 'value' = median arrival year (calendar year). Loss-of-control questions differ: extinction (XPT), catastrophe killing over 10% (XPT, LEAP), extinction or permanent severe disempowerment (ESPAI), 95%+ population decline (Metaculus chain). XPT forecasts are from Jun-Oct 2022; ESPAI 2024 was surveyed Dec 2024 and published Sep 2026.

Fair-disagreement summary: superforecasters (XPT) are roughly an order of magnitude below domain experts on AI extinction, and below AI researchers' survey medians (5-10%). FRI found that forecasters better at predicting others' views gave lower risk estimates. ESPAI found 12% of researchers give zero chance and a third give at least 20%. The International AI Safety Report 2026 gives no consensus number and says expert opinion varies greatly.

Not verified / not used: any 2035 superintelligence probability from Manifold; a Metaculus question asking directly for AI-caused extinction by 2100; the release date of the FLI Statement on Superintelligence (page shows 79,072 signatures but no date).
